data.source_title: Turning Over Patient Turnover: An Ethnographic Study of Admissions, Discharges, and Transfers
data.locator: Results, Table 1 and paragraph beginning 'There were 3562 events on the medical unit'
data.source_setting: One medical and one surgical inpatient unit at a U.S. hospital; institution name is not identified in the article text reviewed.
data.source_period: Turnover records for 2009; one year of admission/discharge records. Ethnographic fieldwork and observation took place on the two units; the paper reports 21 formal interviews among 58 nurses featured in the analysis.
data.source_n: Medical unit: 1,657 admissions and 1,905 discharges in 2009; 3,562 total events. Surgical unit separately had 1,893 admissions and 1,948 discharges. The source table reports events/day, but does not state the number of daily observations used for its mean.
data.quantity: Mean daily medical-unit turnover events (admissions plus discharges, including transfers-in/out)
data.source_evidence_basis: Author summary of unit-level 2009 admission and discharge records; daily event counts are observed administrative records.
data.limitations: One medical unit at a U.S. hospital whose name is not given in the article text reviewed; old single-year data. The table reports 9.95 events/day, but does not state the number of observed unit-days in that mean; dividing 3,562 by 365 gives about 9.76, so do not recompute or assume a 365-day denominator. Event counts do not measure duration or acuity-adjusted workload. Transfers-in are grouped with admissions and transfers-out with discharges.
data.inferred_scenario_use: A workload scenario may represent admissions/discharges/transfers as separate events and sample medical-unit daily event volume around this source-specific distribution; do not use as local throughput or as service minutes.

data.source_title: Turning Over Patient Turnover: An Ethnographic Study of Admissions, Discharges, and Transfers
data.locator: Results, Turnover timing; Table 3, day-to-night shift change (17:30–21:00)
data.source_setting: One medical and one surgical inpatient unit at a U.S. hospital; institution name is not identified in the article text reviewed.
data.source_n: Surgical unit: 487 of 3,841 turnover events in this interval; medical unit: 678 of 3,562 events.
data.quantity: Share of all unit turnover events occurring during 17:30–21:00 day-to-night shift change
data.source_evidence_basis: Observed administrative event timestamps tabulated by unit and time window; table shows 13% surgical and 19% medical for this interval.
data.limitations: Two units in one hospital and one historical year; the table percentages are rounded. Turnover events include admissions and discharges, with transfers included in those categories.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Can test shift-change clustering as a workload sensitivity case, preserving distinct medical and surgical profiles and requiring local event-time data for calibration.
